summary: A Yes vote creates a special parcel tax of $0.06 per square foot of residential improvements and $0.09 per square foot of non-residential improvements for six years, estimated to raise about $9.2 million the first year, to capitalize and support a public bank funding affordable housing, green energy and infrastructure, and small businesses.

tax.text: A Yes vote would impose a temporary six-year parcel tax to raise money for a public bank.
tax.quote: The ballot initiative, if passed, would raise the funds to start the public bank through a temporary six year parcel tax of $0.06 on dwelling units and $0.09 on commercial properties in Berkeley.

energy.text: A Yes vote would fund a public bank intended to invest in green energy solutions and infrastructure.
energy.quote: A public bank takes public money that the city has from taxes and fees and puts it into a government- owned institution where the money is allocated towards affordable housing, green energy solutions, and supporting local businesses.

tax.text: A No vote on Measure Z would reject the six-year parcel tax proposed to capitalize and support a regional public bank.
tax.quote: Creates a parcel tax based on parcel size to help capitalize and support a proposed public bank
